newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander outpaces, mkt awaits buy details.
newsitem.headline: Santander outpaces, mkt awaits buy details.

text.p: Shares in Spain's leading bank Santander continued to outpace the market on Tuesday, as analysts awaited details on what many suspected was a major purchase in Argentina.
"This is an important transaction...It (Santander) hasn't had a major presence there," an analyst said.

Earlier, Santander said it had signed an agreement to take control of Banco Rio de la Plata of Argentina, but reserved details on the size of the stake and the price for a joint announcement at 1400 GMT.
Market sources said the deal could exceed rival Banco Bilbao Vizcaya's recent $600 million purchase for control of Banco de Credito Argentino.
Shares in the group rose 280 pesetas, or 2.22 percent, to 12,880, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up just 1.38 percent. Santander outraced the market on Monday as well.
"It's (the rise) got nothing to do with it. It was already up over two percent this morning," a Spanish bank dealer said.
On Monday, Santander rose sharply after news of cost savings expected from a plan to unify treasury, asset management and corporate business.

"Santander's been going up massively for a long time and its very near our (revised) year-end target of 13,055 pesetas, but also there's been a whole series of rumours about what it's going to do with (unit) Banesto," the dealer said.

Santander Investment, its investment banking arm, has been active in Argentinian business for several years, but despite the bank's recent Latin American buying spree it has purchased no banks in that country.
"It isn't surprising since they're expanding in the area," another analyst said.
